1.explanation:
• src/languages/elixir.js defines Elixir’s syntax rules, including how sigils and operators should be recognized. It currently does not distinguish the slash in function‐capture notation (“&name?/arity”) from the slash that begins a regex. That file must be updated so that ‘&…/⟨number⟩’ is picked up as a capture, not a regex delimiter.  
• src/lib/regex.js implements the generic slash‐vs-regex detection that all languages in Highlight.js inherit. The bug arises because that logic is over-eager with Elixir’s slash, so a small exception or context-check needs to be added there (e.g. don’t start a regex if the slash follows an ampersand and a number).
1.bug_scenario: When you highlight an Elixir snippet that uses the function‐capture shorthand (“&letter?/1”), the highlighter sees the “/” after the “1” as the start of a regex literal and colors everything until the next “/” as if it were a regex. That throws off the rest of the highlighting. In other words “&letter?/1” gets split – the “/1” is treated like “/…/” (a regex) rather than part of a capture expression.

2.explanation: The only place Elixir-specific highlighting rules live is in src/languages/elixir.js. Inside that file it currently pulls in the generic hljs.REGEXP_MODE (slash-delimited regex) even though Elixir’s regex is always introduced by a sigil (~r). Because of this, the standalone “/” in the capture operator (&..?/arity) is being mistaken for the start of a regex. Removing or constraining the REGEXP_MODE entry (or adding logic to ignore a slash immediately following a '?') in elixir.js will prevent the function-capture slash from being highlighted as a regular expression literal.
2.bug_scenario: When highlighting Elixir code that uses the function-capture syntax (&letter?/1), the highlighter sees the “/” in “?/1” as the start of a regex literal and treats everything up to the next slash as part of that regex. As a result, the rest of the line ("/1)") is mis-colored until the following slash, breaking the intended syntax highlighting for the capture operator.
